AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a pest problem for ripe fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Fruit flies and birds
   C. Sun
   D. Stones

2. About how big should a planting hole for a fruit tree be? (1 mark)
   A. 10 cm wide only
   B. About half a metre wide and deep
   C. As big as a football field
   D. About 1 cm

3. Which nutrient in oranges and guavas helps the body to heal cuts and fight colds? (1 mark)
   A. Starch
   B. Vitamin C
   C. Cooking oil
   D. Salt

4. Why do some farmers tie a young tree to a stake? (1 mark)
   A. To keep it upright in wind
   B. To make it thicker
   C. To feed it
   D. To stop it growing

5. What is the young one of a goat called? (1 mark)
   A. Chick
   B. Lamb
   C. Calf
   D. Kid

6. Which nutrient in eggs helps the body to grow? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar only
   B. Salt
   C. Protein
   D. Starch only

7. What is the young one of a sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Kid
   B. Lamb
   C. Foal
   D. Calf

8. Which animal is kept mainly for wool? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Goat
   C. Donkey
   D. Wool sheep

9. Why is a meal of only chips not balanced? (1 mark)
   A. It has too many vegetables
   B. It lacks body-building and protective foods
   C. It has no energy
   D. It has too much protein

10. Which of these is a body-building food? (1 mark)
   A. Rice
   B. Chapati
   C. Cooking oil
   D. Beans

11. Which of these root foods gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Sweet potato
   B. Kale
   C. Milk
   D. Egg

12. Which of these gives fibre? (1 mark)
   A. Sweets
   B. Vegetables and fruits
   C. Soft drinks
   D. Sugar

13. Why should the frying pan be heated before adding food? (1 mark)
   A. To break it
   B. To melt it
   C. To burn it
   D. So that food browns and does not soak up oil

14. Who should be with a child who is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. An adult
   B. Nobody
   C. A friend only
   D. A younger child

15. Why should vegetables be boiled for a short time only? (1 mark)
   A. Long boiling makes them colder
   B. Short boiling makes them poisonous
   C. It saves nothing
   D. Long boiling destroys some vitamins

16. How much oil is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. None
   B. A whole bottle
   C. A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   D. A full pot

17. How can you make drinking water safe? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it in the sun uncovered
   B. Stir it with a stick
   C. Add soil
   D. Boil it and let it cool covered

18. Which disease can be spread by dirty hands? (1 mark)
   A. Broken leg
   B. Diarrhoea
   C. Sunburn
   D. Toothache only

19. What can be used if there is no soap? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar
   B. Oil
   C. Mud
   D. Clean ash and running water

20. How does the tippy tap release water? (1 mark)
   A. By a magnet
   B. By a switch
   C. A foot lever tips the container
   D. By a battery

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to wash hands correctly. (4 marks)

22. Plan a balanced supper using local foods and name the group of each food. (3 marks)

23. Describe how a group can share the work of growing a fruit tree at school. (4 marks)

24. Name three foods that are boiled. (3 marks)

25. Describe how to shallow fry an egg. (4 marks)

26. Name the young of a cow, a goat and a sheep. (3 marks)

27. Describe the first aid for a small burn. (3 marks)

28. Explain four things that may happen to a child who does not eat a balanced diet. (4 marks)

29. Explain what is meant by a balanced meal. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Fruit flies and birds
   Ripe fruit attracts flies and birds.

2. B — About half a metre wide and deep
   The hole gives roots space in loose soil.

3. B — Vitamin C
   Vitamin C helps the body fight illness.

4. A — To keep it upright in wind
   Stakes protect against bending.

5. D — Kid
   A young goat is a kid.

6. C — Protein
   Eggs are body-building foods.

7. B — Lamb
   A young sheep is a lamb.

8. D — Wool sheep
   Some sheep breeds have wool.

9. B — It lacks body-building and protective foods
   Chips give mainly energy.

10. D — Beans
   Beans have protein.

11. A — Sweet potato
   Sweet potatoes are starchy.

12. B — Vegetables and fruits
   Fibre helps digestion.

13. D — So that food browns and does not soak up oil
   Food placed in cold oil soaks up oil.

14. A — An adult
   An adult helps prevent accidents.

15. D — Long boiling destroys some vitamins
   Vitamins are lost with too much cooking.

16. C — A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer.

17. D — Boil it and let it cool covered
   Boiling kills germs.

18. B — Diarrhoea
   Germs on hands can get into the mouth.

19. D — Clean ash and running water
   Ash helps to remove dirt when soap is not available.

20. C — A foot lever tips the container
   Pushing the lever tips the container.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wet hands; use soap; rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs and nails for about 20 seconds; rinse; dry with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example, rice (energy), fish (body-building), spinach (protective).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food correctly named and placed.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a chart with jobs such as watering, weeding, mulching and recording; take turns each week; check the plant daily; record dates of flowers and fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity or arrangement.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes, eggs, cassava, maize, beans, rice (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Crack the egg into a bowl; heat a little oil in the pan; slide the egg in; cook until the white is firm; lift out with a spatula.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Calf, kid and lamb.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the burn under cool running clean water for at least ten minutes, cover it loosely with a clean cloth and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Weakness, tiredness, frequent illness, slow growth, poor concentration (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: A meal that has foods from all the main food groups in the right amounts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for foods from all groups, 1 mark for right amounts.
